blocks.text: Although it is named for the Florida Keys, other locations, particularly Coney Island and Myrtle Beach, serve as inspiration for the aesthetic. Like many other online aesthetics, Key West Kitten has become subject to mass-tagging, meaning that vaguely-related or unrelated images will often appear in search results for it. Likewise, it is sometimes used interchangeably with the names of other, related aesthetics, particularly Coconut Girl and Tropicalcore.

Key West Kitten was first coined by blogger/influencer Alida Simone, who gained prominence within the Nymphet, Coquette, and Trailer Park Princess communities in around 2016 under the username @babydarkoangel. It is unknown when exactly the aesthetic originated, as some of its most popular images are from the 2000s or even earlier, but by the time the name Key West Kitten was (most likely) coined in 2017, it was quite prevalent on Pinterest and Tumblr. Before the name was coined, bloggers would often simply tag their photos with Lizzy Grant-related hashtags such as #wayamaya and #mermaid motel.

Regarding the aesthetic, Simone herself has stated that Key West Kitten wasn't an aesthetic for her, and was just her and her life, and that the name Key West Kitten was what her mother would sometimes call her due to the fact that the Florida Keys are where she and Simone's father first fell in love. However, she does find it beautiful that a community was built around something so special to her.

Sometime in the early 2020s, a similar aesthetic to Key West Kitten emerged which contained far more bright colors, Y2K fashion, and references to 2000s media, and boomed in popularity on sites such as TikTok and Instagram. It became known as Coconut Girl, although neither it nor the earlier Key West Kitten were ever in the spotlight very long. Now, the names are used somewhat interchangeably on some sites, but remain distinct on others. While Coconut Girl received enough attention to have multiple online articles about it, and inspired some brands to make more tropical-patterned clothing, the name Key West Kitten, and its associated aesthetic, remained relatively obscure and restricted to Tumblr and Pinterest.

Some members of the community have also mixed it with Gyaru and its substyles, particularly Manba, due to the fact they blend beachy or tropical themes with Camp and Kitsch ones. It is also somewhat related to Gloomy Coquette in that it also utilizes filters and desaturated colors to create a nostalgic, hazy atmosphere, like a childhood dream.

Key West Kitten visuals heavily rely on the pastel blue-pink-yellow color palette, and a general air of femininity, summertime, and carefree fun. Because these matter more than the subject matter of the images, members of the community post a somewhat wide variety of photos, including people, clothing, food, nature, and manmade structures. It is very common to see collages and long photosets in the Key West Kitten hashtag on Tumblr.
